CVE-2026-121750.title: nvm install --offline installs a cached tarball that previously failed checksum verification
CVE-2026-121750.description: Node Version Manager (nvm) is a POSIX-compliant shell function for managing multiple node.js versions. In versions 0.40.5 through 0.40.8, `nvm_download_artifact` downloads a release archive directly to its final path in `$NVM_DIR/.cache` and verifies its checksum afterwards; on a checksum mismatch it reports an error but leaves the rejected archive in place. A later `nvm install --offline` of the same version installs that cached file without a checksum, so an archive that was just rejected gets installed and its `node` and `npm` run. This gives code execution to a party who can alter the downloaded tarball (for example a poisoned CDN or cache object) but cannot also forge the `SHASUMS256.txt` beside it, if the victim runs `nvm install --offline` for that version after the visible "Checksums do not match" failure and before any online retry. Version 0.41.0 only puts an archive in the cache once its checksum has passed.

CVE-2026-126188.title: Active Storage: Possible local file disclosure in Active Storage video previews and analysis
CVE-2026-126188.description: Active Storage makes it simple to upload and reference files in cloud services and attach those files to Active Record objects. Prior to 8.0.5.2 and from 8.1 until 8.1.4.1, Active Storage's ActiveStorage::Previewer::VideoPreviewer, ActiveStorage::Analyzer::VideoAnalyzer, and ActiveStorage::Analyzer::AudioAnalyzer pass uploaded blob contents to FFmpeg without restricting the demuxer. This issue is fixed in versions 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1.

CVE-2026-128076.title: Nuxt: Colliding island props can share one `/__nuxt_island` path (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-46342)
CVE-2026-128076.description: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 3.21.6 to before 4.0.0 and from 4.4.6 until 4.6.4, the /__nuxt_island path hash uses ohash serialization that does not escape quotes in string values or delimiters in object keys, allowing different island-prop tuples to produce the same path. For prerendering, substituted content is written into the generated page only if the crawler reaches a colliding URL before rendering the page with the legitimate props. Separately, a CDN or reverse proxy that keys island responses by path alone can be primed with the colliding response. If the substituted prop reaches v-html, innerHTML, or another unsafe HTML sink, the response can execute script in the application origin; otherwise the impact is content substitution. Applications that do not use server components or NuxtIsland, islands without attacker-influenced string props, and responses not cached by path alone are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

CVE-2026-99222.title: keys: Protect the read method check against type removal
CVE-2026-99222.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

keys: Protect the read method check against type removal

keyctl_read_key() checks key->type->read without holding key->sem.
A reference keeps the key alive, but does not pin the module containing
its type. A surviving RxRPC key can therefore be read while AF_RXRPC
is being unloaded:

KEYCTL_READ task Module unload and key GC
---------------- ------------------------
lookup_user_key()
permission / possession checks
load key->type
af_rxrpc_exit()
unregister_key_type()
GC: down_write(key->sem)
GC: retype to key_type_dead
GC: up_write(key->sem)
unregister_key_type() returns
free_module()
read saved type's read member

The final access can read freed module storage. The read invocation in
__keyctl_read_key() is already protected by key->sem, but the earlier
method check is outside that critical section.

Move the method check into __keyctl_read_key(), after key_validate() and
under its existing read hold on key->sem.…
